16:15.reflection: Are the believers closest to me, including my own household, being encouraged in their faith?
16:15.action: Pray by name for the families in your congregation today, and check in on one household that may need encouragement or practical help.
16:15.prayer: Gracious Father, thank You for the saints who gather in homes and families, for faith passed between parents and children. Bless the households of Your church and knit us together in love and peace. Amen.

16:16.devotion: Paul instructs the Romans to greet one another with a holy kiss, a customary sign of warm, pure affection among believers in that culture, and passes along greetings from the churches of Christ. The gospel created real, affectionate community. Christian fellowship was never meant to be cold or merely formal.
16:16.reflection: Do my greetings and presence communicate genuine warmth and love to my brothers and sisters in Christ?
16:16.action: Offer a warm, culturally fitting greeting today, such as a handshake, hug, or kind word, to fellow believers and newcomers alike.
16:16.prayer: Lord Jesus, You have joined us into one family across every background. Make our fellowship warm and sincere. Let my greetings and friendships reflect Your love, and unite Your churches in genuine affection. Amen.

16:17.devotion: After warm greetings, Paul offers a sober warning. He urges the Romans to watch for those who cause divisions and stumbling blocks contrary to the teaching they had received, and to avoid them. Unity in Christ is precious, but it must not be preserved by tolerating teaching that overturns the gospel they had learned.
16:17.reflection: Am I discerning about teachings that stir division, or do I accept every claim without testing it against Scripture?
16:17.action: Review a core doctrine of your faith in Scripture today, and if you encounter divisive teaching, respond with gentle, clear truth rather than gossip.
16:17.prayer: Father, give me discernment to recognize teaching that divides Your people and distorts the gospel. Keep me rooted in the truth I have learned from Your Word, and make me a peacemaker who holds fast to Christ. Amen.

16:18.devotion: Paul explains why such people are dangerous: they serve their own appetites rather than the Lord, and they win followers through smooth, flattering words that deceive the unwary. The warning is pastoral, calling believers to weigh character and message together, not merely eloquence or charm.
16:18.reflection: Am I measuring teachers by their character and faithfulness to Christ, or by their persuasiveness and charm?
16:18.action: Before accepting or sharing a teaching or message this week, pause to examine it against Scripture and the character of the one delivering it.
16:18.prayer: Lord, protect me from smooth words that flatter but do not serve You. Give me a heart that loves truth, eyes that test all teaching by Your Word, and discernment to follow Christ alone. Amen.

16:19.devotion: Paul rejoices that the Romans' obedience has become known everywhere. Then he gives his desire for them: be wise in what is good, and simple, or innocent, concerning evil. Mature faith is not worldly cleverness about sin but deep, practiced goodness that leaves little room for evil to gain a foothold.
16:19.reflection: Am I growing wise and practiced in goodness, or dangerously curious about evil?
16:19.action: Choose one good practice, such as honesty, generosity, or prayer, and deliberately strengthen it today instead of entertaining a compromise you have been tempted by.
16:19.prayer: Father, thank You for the obedience You have worked in me so far. Make me wise in all that is good and innocent toward evil. Let my life be known for goodness that honors Christ. Amen.

16:20.devotion: Paul closes his letter with a confident promise: the God of peace, not our own strength, will decisively defeat Satan, and the victory is near. Believers share in that triumph under Christ's grace. We fight from assurance, not anxiety, knowing evil's end is already determined.
16:20.reflection: Where in your life do you need to remember that God Himself is fighting for you rather than trusting your own strength?
16:20.action: Name one fear or temptation that feels overwhelming today, then hand it to God in prayer and take one obedient step against it.
16:20.prayer: God of peace, thank You that Satan's defeat is certain and near. Keep me standing in Your grace today, unafraid of the enemy, resting in the victory You have already secured. Amen.

16:21.devotion: As Paul closes his letter to Rome, he passes along greetings from coworkers traveling with him. Timothy, his longtime companion in ministry, and Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, fellow Jews, join in greeting the Roman believers. Even a letter of deep theology is deeply personal, carried by real friendships forged in shared service to Christ.
16:21.reflection: Who are the coworkers God has placed beside me in my walk of faith?
16:21.action: Send a message of appreciation today to one person who has served alongside you in faith or ministry.
16:21.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for the friends and coworkers You have given me in the faith. Help me to value them, encourage them, and serve alongside them with a grateful heart. Amen.

16:22.devotion: Here a voice suddenly speaks in the first person: Tertius, the scribe who took Paul's dictation, adds his own greeting in the Lord. This small detail reminds us that Scripture came through ordinary human hands. Tertius served faithfully behind the scenes, and his work became part of inspired Scripture.
16:22.reflection: Am I willing to serve faithfully even when my part remains mostly unseen?
16:22.action: Do one behind-the-scenes task today, like washing dishes or organizing supplies, without seeking recognition for it.
16:22.prayer: Father, thank You for quiet servants like Tertius whose faithful work blesses others. Teach me to serve You willingly in hidden places, content that You see and know my heart. Amen.

16:23.devotion: Paul sends greetings from his hosts in Corinth. Gaius opened his home not just to Paul but to the whole church, showing generous hospitality. Erastus, the city treasurer, demonstrates that faith reached people of public standing, while Quartus is simply called a brother. The church gathered rich and ordinary lives alike around one table.
16:23.reflection: Is my home and my life open enough for others in the church to find welcome there?
16:23.action: Invite someone from church or your neighborhood to share a simple meal or coffee with you this week.
16:23.prayer: Lord, thank You for believers like Gaius who make room for others. Give me a hospitable heart and an open door, that Your people may find welcome and encouragement with me. Amen.

16:24.devotion: Paul's closing benediction is brief and rich: a request that the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with all the believers in Rome. Grace is not a formula Paul recites; it is his deepest longing for the church. He ends where the gospel begins, resting everything on God's unearned favor toward us in Christ.
16:24.reflection: Do I genuinely desire God's grace for others, even those I find difficult?
16:24.action: Speak or write a word of blessing over one person today, asking God's grace to be with them.
16:24.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for Your grace that sustains me daily. Let that grace rest on my family, my church, and even those who challenge me, binding us together in Your love. Amen.

16:25.devotion: Paul bursts into a doxology, praising the God who is able to establish believers through the gospel he preaches. He speaks of a mystery hidden through long ages, God's saving plan in Christ, now revealed. The same God who kept this promise secret has now made it known, and He is able to make His people stand firm in it.
16:25.reflection: Where do I need God to establish and steady me in my faith right now?
16:25.action: Memorize one short gospel verse today and repeat it whenever you feel anxious or unsteady.
16:25.prayer: God of wisdom, You are able to establish me through the gospel of Jesus Christ. When I waver, root me in Your revealed plan of salvation and keep me standing firm in Your truth. Amen.

16:26.devotion: The mystery once hidden is now made manifest, Paul continues, revealed through the prophetic Scriptures and made known to all nations. God's command stands behind this worldwide disclosure, and its goal is obedience to the faith. The gospel is not private information; it is good news intended to reach every people and produce trusting obedience.
16:26.reflection: Is the good news I have received flowing out of my life toward people who have not heard it?
16:26.action: Share one sentence about what Christ means to you with a friend, coworker, or family member today.
16:26.prayer: Everlasting God, thank You for making Your saving plan known through the Scriptures to all nations. Use my ordinary words and witness to spread obedience of faith where I live. Amen.

16:27.devotion: Paul's letter ends where all things should end: with glory to God. He praises the alone-wise God, whose wisdom devised salvation, and directs that glory through Jesus Christ forever. After sixteen chapters of doctrine, correction, and greetings, the final word is worship, for the gospel's purpose is ultimately to magnify God.
16:27.reflection: Does my life, with all its busyness, actually end in praise to God?
16:27.action: Pause for two minutes today to deliberately praise God aloud for His wisdom in your salvation.
16:27.prayer: Alone-wise God, all glory belongs to You through Jesus Christ, forever. Receive my praise today, and let my whole life, in its words and works, point back to Your wisdom and grace. Amen.
